content: mbc6test is a CGB-only Game Boy Color conformance-test ROM for MBC6 mapper implementations. The documented scope excludes DMG/MGB/SGB and dual-mode support; verification must distinguish static build invariants from runtime mapper correctness.
title: MBC6 test ROM target is CGB-only

content: The project memory model specifies independent 8 KiB ROM/Flash windows at $4000-$5FFF and $6000-$7FFF, and independent 4 KiB SRAM windows at $A000-$AFFF and $B000-$BFFF. ROM bank numbers use 8 KiB units; SRAM bank numbers use 4 KiB units; bank 0 is valid in the switchable ROM windows.
title: MBC6 independent windows and bank units

content: The project's source-precedence policy puts current Pan Docs first for specified MBC6/CGB behavior, iceboy flash documentation next for MX29F008TC/ATC details, then GBDev research observations for unresolved behavior. Existing emulator behavior and other test ROMs are not hardware specifications. Keep uncertain observations as INFO rather than normative PASS/FAIL expectations.
title: MBC6 evidence must follow source precedence

content: The default build must not expose flash erase/program/protect/unprotect paths. Destructive tests are compile-time disabled by default and require explicit multi-button confirmation when enabled. The project states that 128 KiB sectors cannot be fully backed up in 32 KiB SRAM, so it cannot promise restoration of arbitrary real-cartridge flash contents.
title: Destructive flash tests stay disabled by default

content: The static ROM verifier checks image size, cartridge header, checksums, and physical-bank signatures. Passing make verify does not demonstrate runtime MBC6 mapper correctness; runtime results must be collected in an emulator or compatible hardware and recorded separately.
title: Static ROM verification is not runtime proof

content: The historical MBC6 research thread reports an apparent high-bank-bit unmapping behavior and Net de Get writes of $C6 to bank source/type registers for unknown reasons. The project keeps these as experimental INFO-only tests and forbids using them as normative behavior without authoritative evidence.
title: Unresolved MBC6 research stays INFO-only

content: The notes report that T31-T33 flash JEDEC-ID tests failed on the tested GBE+ and mGBA builds because flash ID readback was not implemented in those emulator sources. Treat this as a version-specific emulator gap, not evidence that the ROM's documented JEDEC expectation is wrong or that real hardware behaves the same way.
title: JEDEC ID failures were traced to tested emulator gaps

content: Project notes report that the same ROM bytes booted in CGB mode in mGBA 0.11 dev when named mbc6-test.gbc, while mbc6-test.gb caused a CGB REQUIRED screen; GBE+ was unaffected. Preserve the .gbc output convention and re-check this behavior against the target emulator version before relying on it.
title: mGBA CGB behavior observed to depend on .gbc extension

content: The project owner identified and the authenticated browser session confirmed this Claude Code session as the primary MBC6Test conversation. Its hosted conversation was reviewed for durable project memory; the raw transcript was not copied into OMM. Related local continuation logs 81880153-b86e-4d1e-a605-e1fe9c128d91 and 95f4383e-23d6-4be5-a216-b2ecaba1e0c6 contain compacted summaries and later exchanges, but are not assumed to be a complete copy of the hosted session.
evidence: Claude Code session visually inspected in authenticated browser on 2026-10-01
title: Archived Claude Code conversation identified as the primary MBC6Test history

content: The project owner rejected treating a successful build as sufficient validation and required real runtime testing. Test outcomes must be human-readable on-screen, including a result grid, failure-detail view, and INFO view, rather than only a one-line summary. Keep static verification and runtime mapper evidence distinct.
title: MBC6Test changes require genuine runtime evidence and readable results

content: Historical implementation work cross-checked behavior against GBE+ and mGBA while preserving emulator limitations as emulator-specific evidence. Do not change normative test expectations to accommodate an emulator gap; identify the emulator and version and report that gap separately. BGB was not treated as a usable MBC6 runtime oracle in that work.
title: Keep emulator gaps separate from normative MBC6 expectations

content: The owner chose a manually triggered GitHub Actions release workflow, with a seven-character commit hash as the release tag and the same build identifier displayed in the ROM title/results UI. Builds should not publish automatically on every push. Gitea is a backup mirror, not the release destination.
title: Release builds are manual GitHub Actions runs with traceable build IDs

content: The default build keeps destructive flash tests disabled. The manual release pipeline also builds and verifies an explicitly enabled destructive configuration and publishes it as a separately named, clearly labeled asset. Keep the default safe ROM and destructive ROM distinguishable in both artifact name and release description.
title: Publish and verify both safe and explicitly destructive configurations

content: The historical discussion clarified that the datasheet linked from the NP GB Memory research page is for AMD/Spansion Am29F400, not the Macronix MX29F008TC/ATC used in the cartridge. It was not the implementation authority; the work relied on the iceboy reverse-engineering notes and cross-checks against hardware tools. Treat command similarities as cross-check context, not proof that the two flash parts are identical.
title: The linked Am29F400 datasheet is analogous, not the MBC6 cartridge flash datasheet

content: The project owner established Brazilian Portuguese as the conversation language. The historical workflow also required explicit user direction before committing or pushing changes; preserve that project-specific preference when working in the MBC6Test repository.
title: Keep MBC6 communication in Brazilian Portuguese and require explicit commit or push requests

content: The archived session reported a historical safe-suite run of 20 tests: 12 PASS, 3 FAIL, and 5 INFO, with screen values independently checked against raw emulator memory. For the opt-in destructive suite, TD4 passed at runtime, TD5 reports INFO and TD6 SKIP by design, while TD1-TD3 remained unconfirmed at runtime because available emulators did not implement the required flash-write behavior correctly. These are historical results, not current-build claims.
evidence: GBE+ and mGBA validation discussed in archived session
title: Safe-suite and destructive-flash runtime results were reported separately

content: The implementation discussion corrected two flash command details after cross-checking shonumi/dandocs, FlashGBX, and sanni/cartreader: the buffered-program commit is a distinct write of literal $00, not a repeated data byte, and the reset command $F0 is issued once per window. The session also applied the confirmed $1000/$0C00 flash enable sequence before destructive operations. Preserve the cited source distinctions and do not infer current implementation state without checking code.
title: Flash buffer commit uses literal zero and reset is issued once

content: The owner supplied Game Boy hardware database photos of two physical MBC6 cartridges. The session reported that both showed the Macronix MX29F008TC-14 flash chip, independently corroborating the project's existing target. The same photos showed a Mitsumi MM1134A supervisor/reset component; its relationship, if any, to MBC6 write protection or register $1000 was explicitly left unknown and was not made normative behavior.
title: Real cartridge photos confirmed the Macronix flash part

content: Photos of two MBC6 cartridges show a Mitsumi MM1134A supervisor/reset component. The archived session found no source proving whether it interacts with MBC6 registers such as $1000 or is only part of independent power/reset protection. Keep this as an explicit unknown; do not encode a software behavior assumption without further hardware evidence.
title: Mitsumi MM1134A role in MBC6 flash write protection is unresolved

content: The project owner asked what the screen status letters mean. The screen guide defines P as PASS, F as FAIL, S as SKIP, I as INFO, and a dash as not run in this build. Preserve this user-facing explanation and distinguish a test that was not compiled into a build from one that passed.
evidence: docs/screen-guide.md status-letters section, as cited in the archived session
title: Explain every on-screen test status and distinguish tests absent from a build

content: The original user specification requires a self-contained 1 MiB CGB-only MBC6 conformance ROM, with unique deterministic signatures for all 128 physical 8 KiB banks and independent tests of both ROM and SRAM windows. Do not broaden the target to DMG/MGB/SGB or dual-mode operation. Test data, graphics, fonts, and fixtures must be generated from source; do not use commercial Net de Get ROM data, copyrighted assets, extracted firmware, or proprietary binaries.
evidence: Claude Code conversation message 1, original project prompt
pinned mbc6test CLAUDE.md and README references imported separately
title: MBC6 conformance ROM scope is CGB-only and covers all 128 physical ROM banks

content: The user specification requires startup, MBC6 register helpers, dispatcher, display, result formatting, input, flash helpers, and core assertions to run from fixed ROM at $0000-$3FFF. Never execute code from a switchable window while remapping that same address space. Flash status polling must have a software timeout, preserve diagnostic status, and continue safely where possible; no test may hang forever.
evidence: Claude Code conversation message 1, sections 6 and 13
title: Mapper-changing routines stay in fixed ROM and flash polling stays bounded
